How tides work

Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun, and the rotation of the Earth.

Key factors

  • The Moon's gravity
  • The Sun's gravity
  • Earth's rotation

HIDDENTEXT

Most coastal areas experience two high tides and two low tides every lunar day, which is about 24 hours and 50 minutes long.
